subject: biology
title: Thermoregulation in Endotherms
explanation: Thermoreceptors in the skin and hypothalamus detect temperature changes and relay information to the thermoregulatory centre in the hypothalamus, which acts as the coordination centre. The hypothalamus compares input against the set point of approximately 37 degrees Celsius and initiates appropriate autonomic responses via the nervous and endocrine systems.
points: When body temperature rises, vasodilation increases blood flow to skin capillaries through relaxation of arteriole smooth muscle, increasing heat loss by radiation, while sweat glands secrete fluid that evaporates and removes latent heat from the skin surface

When body temperature falls, vasoconstriction reduces blood flow to the skin by contraction of arteriole smooth muscle minimising heat loss, shivering generates heat through involuntary muscle contractions, and erector pili muscles contract causing piloerection though this is ineffective in humans
The hypothalamus also regulates metabolic rate through thyroid hormone release, with increased thyroxine production raising cellular respiration and heat generation during prolonged cold exposure
summary: The hypothalamus receives temperature information from peripheral and central thermoreceptors, then activates appropriate effectors like sweat glands, arterioles, or skeletal muscles to adjust heat production or loss.
exam: Examiners expect students to distinguish between behavioral and physiological responses and to explain vasodilation versus vasoconstriction mechanisms in blood vessels near the skin surface.
